paper.title_en: Deformation and Magicity in Heavy Actinides: First Observation of the Ground-State Rotational Band of <math display="inline"><mrow><mmultiscripts><mrow><mi>Fm</mi></mrow><mprescripts/><none/><mrow><mn>252</mn></mrow></mmultiscripts></mrow></math>
paper.abstract_en: The ground-state rotational band of <math display="inline"><mrow><mmultiscripts><mrow><mi>Fm</mi></mrow><mprescripts/><none/><mrow><mn>252</mn></mrow></mmultiscripts></mrow></math> (<math display="inline"><mi>Z</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>100</mn></math>, <math display="inline"><mi>N</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>152</mn></math>) was investigated using two different experimental setups at the JAEA Tandem Accelerator Laboratory. The <math display="inline"><mrow><msup><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow><mrow><mo>+</mo></mrow></msup><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><msup><mrow><mn>0</mn></mrow><mrow><mo>+</mo></mrow></msup></mrow></math> and <math display="inline"><msup><mn>4</mn><mo>+</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><msup><mn>2</mn><mo>+</mo></msup></math> transitions were observed in the <math display="inline"><mi>α</mi></math> decay of <math display="inline"><mrow><mmultiscripts><mrow><mi>No</mi></mrow><mprescripts/><none/><mrow><mn>256</mn></mrow></mmultiscripts></mrow></math> via <math display="inline"><mrow><mi>α</mi><mtext>-</mtext><mi>γ</mi></mrow></math> coincidence spectroscopy. The energies of the <math display="inline"><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mrow><mn>6</mn></mrow><mrow><mo>+</mo></mrow></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mrow><mn>4</mn></mrow><mrow><mo>+</mo></mrow></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>, <math display="inline"><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mn>8</mn><mo>+</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mn>6</mn><mo>+</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></math>, and <math display="inline"><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><msup><mn>0</mn><mo>+</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mn>8</mn><mo>+</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></math> transitions were identified in the prompt <math display="inline"><mi>γ</mi></math>-ray spectrum of <math display="inline"><mrow><mmultiscripts><mrow><mi>Fm</mi></mrow><mprescripts/><none/><mrow><mn>252</mn></mrow></mmultiscripts></mrow></math> produced in the <math display="inline"><mrow><mmultiscripts><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi></mrow><mprescripts/><none/><mrow><mn>18</mn></mrow></mmultiscripts><mo>+</mo><mrow><mmultiscripts><mrow><mi>Cf</mi></mrow><mprescripts/><none/><mrow><mn>249</mn></mrow></mmultiscripts></mrow></mrow></math> multinucleon transfer reaction. The new data reveal that, compared with neighboring fermium isotopes and <math display="inline"><mi>N</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>152</mn></math> isotones in the region, <math display="inline"><mrow><mmultiscripts><mrow><mi>Fm</mi></mrow><mprescripts/><none/><mrow><mn>252</mn></mrow></mmultiscripts></mrow></math> has the lowest first excited <math display="inline"><msup><mn>2</mn><mo>+</mo></msup></math>-state energy, 41.88(16) keV, and the largest kinematic moment of inertia. These properties constitute new evidence for the deformed shell gaps at <math display="inline"><mi>Z</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>100</mn></math> and <math display="inline"><mi>N</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>152</mn></math>, supporting the understanding of <math display="inline"><mrow><mmultiscripts><mrow><mi>Fm</mi></mrow><mprescripts/><none/><mrow><mn>252</mn></mrow></mmultiscripts></mrow></math> as a deformed doubly magic nucleus.
